suggestion: From a session on cl45: kit.py done cl45 (commits after proof are files-map only), then kit.py land cl45 (carries cl51).
text:
**continue** (rechecked at 9db1f49, the joint CL45+CL51 fix) · Land cl45, which carries cl51, as one landing. In the same go, make the web review launch run `kit.py review <post> --session-id <the new session's id>`, so the new no-push guard can see a review.

## Recheck at b14a977 (cl45 with main merged again, CL55 included)
- The commits since the proof (743eb93) are 9db1f49, 9c213ac and b14a977, all generated files-map changes (`.kit/artifact-files/files-board.json`), plus merges of main. The seeded-conflict script still gives 5 of 5 kept or standing, and the CL45 and CL51 checks pass. The verdict stays **continue**.
- I did **not land** it. `land` refuses commits made after the proof. `kit.py done` checks the checkout it runs in, so from this review branch it refuses: the CL51 test file is not on this branch, and main has moved. Running it on cl45 would mean taking the part over, which this session's permissions refused. The fix: `kit.py done cl45-…` from a session on cl45 (its part, or the orchestrator), then `kit.py land cl45-…`.

## Recheck of the commits after 9db1f49 (origin/cl45 at 9c213ac)
- Since 9db1f49, cl45 has a merge of origin/main (CL48, already reviewed and landed as 01b49ab), c4ad7d3 (an empty "checkpoint(cl45): save progress"), and **9c213ac**, which only removes 4 lines from the generated `.kit/artifact-files/files-board.json`. No kit code or test changed beyond what main already holds. The verdict stays **continue**.
- `kit.py land` still refuses: "1 commit(s) on cl45 after its review (9c213ac)". Its proof is at 743eb93. The fix is `kit.py done cl45-…` by its part or the orchestrator, then land. I did not run `done`: it is the part's command, and a review never takes a part over.
- With CL55 now landed, this is the pattern CR-cl55 names: a files-map or checkpoint commit after the review blocks land.

## Recheck after the joint fix (origin/cl45 at 9db1f49, which has origin/cl51 merged in, fix 743eb93)
- `scripts/review/CR-cl45-a-web-session-reconciles-its-artifact-wi-seeded-conflict.py`, all 5 cases now pass: new container and same container, GitHub newer and web newer. Each keeps both copies, with one conflict comment, and a reopen made on the Artifact stands (in progress on the board and in git). Before the fix, 3 of these lost on the merge and 2 lost on cl45 alone.
- `tests.test_cl45_artifact_reconcile` and `tests.test_cl51_computer_artifact` both pass (the CL45 file now has the seeded cases as tests).
- Merged with cl53 (c42c0dc): one conflict, in the generated `.kit/artifact-files/files-board.json` files map only. With it resolved, `run_all_tests.py --all` gives **73 passed, 0 failed**.
- How it was fixed: reconcile now takes the Artifact's side from the raw pulled files, read before the load, so CL51's `keep_newer` can no longer hide a change. The computer half of CL51 is unchanged.
- **The review guard, partly held.** A web review now never pushes board-mirror when a post it pulls has `review_session` equal to this session's id (`kit.py whoami`, here `session_01AE…`). That field is written only by `kit.py review <post> --session-id …`. None of the three posts carried it when this review session started, so the guard would not have stopped this session's push (d0c649c). It holds only if the web review launch records the id.
- Not checked: a real both-sides conflict on Harmonize's data (there is still none in the data).

The text below is the first review (redirect), kept as written.

~~**redirect** · Launch one fix step for CL45 and CL51 together (it lands both): `artifact reconcile` decides each post from the Artifact's raw pulled copy, not from the local board after CL51's `keep_newer` load, and its test seeds the local board from git first, with both dates (git newer, web newer), plus a reopen made on the Artifact.~~

## Holds
**On its own branch (cl45 at ee7e993): yes.**
- Check rerun: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_cl45_artifact_reconcile`: 3 of 3 pass, with and without the web flag.
- Break rerun (its `breaks` sed in a scratch worktree): the check fails (1 failure), so the check can fail. Undone with the worktree.
- Recheck sample, "a both-sides change kept twice, a second run adds no second conflict comment": rerun inside its test, and again in my own script on a new web container (the local board seeded from git, the kit's Artifact state gone): on cl45 alone both copies are kept, whichever side is newer.

**Merged with CL51 (cl45+cl51+cl53, the orchestrator's merge rebuilt here as f6fd14d, clean): no.** CL45's main promise breaks there. Measured by `scripts/review/CR-cl45-a-web-session-reconciles-its-artifact-wi-seeded-conflict.py` (run it from a checkout's root):

| case (local board seeded from git, as web_takeover does) | cl45 alone | cl45+cl51 |
|---|---|---|
| new container, both changed, GitHub newer | both kept, 1 conflict comment | **web's edit LOST**: no conflict comment, git's copy shown and queued for the Artifact |
| new container, both changed, web newer | both kept | both kept |
| a step reopened on the Artifact (complete to in progress, newer) | stands | **undone**: back to complete on the board, in git, then on the Artifact |
| same container (kit state kept), both changed | LOST (either date) | LOST (either date) |

Why: CL51's `keep_newer` now runs inside `artifact_load`. At a real web start the local board already holds git's copy, so the load keeps it when it is newer and never lowers a status. Reconcile then sees local == git, finds no conflict, and `artifact push` sends git's copy over the Artifact's. CL45's own test never seeds the local board before the load (its second test does, but with no both-sides change), so it does not see this.

The last row is CL45's own gap, older than CL51: in a container that kept `.kit/run/artifact/base`, the git seed counts as a local edit and `_merge_fields` puts it over the Artifact's copy.

**A review wrote board-mirror.** This review session ran the hook's WEB steps (`web_takeover.py`, then `artifact reconcile`), and that pushed origin/board-mirror (d0c649c, "30 to git": M5 to M8 reviews, cards, this post). The rule "a review never writes the git copy" depends on `KIT_ROLE`, and the kit's web review launch does not set it. The content was additive. This also answers the handoff's question in practice: a web session does push board-mirror today, a review included.

**Real project** (orchestrator, Harmonize, post's real_project): reconcile rc=0 with KIT_NO_BOARD_PUSH, 8 to GitHub, 0 conflicts; "a both-sides conflict (none in the data)" not met. The case that breaks has never run on real data.

Not checked: a real push from the orchestrator's own web start (only mine, above); the Artifact page on a phone.

## Goal
The board-data train serves one thing: the board is the same wherever the owner opens it (phone Artifact, computer, GitHub), and nothing anyone wrote is lost (CL16's goal). The measure so far is unit tests on temp repos plus one dry run with no conflict in the data. That is a stand-in: the failure the owner actually met (20:23Z, 11 posts rolled back) came from two writers meeting, and this merge creates a new meeting point that no test covers.

Together the posts show this: CL51's handoff says CL45 "can rely on" "load never writes an older copy over a newer one". CL45 relies on the opposite: the load must hand it the Artifact's copy as it is, so that it can tell who changed what. Each is right alone. Together they lose an edit silently, which is the exact thing CL45 was asked never to do.

No post records the owner checking the result himself on his phone since the 20:23Z damage.

## Verdict
**redirect.** Do not land CL45 and CL51 as they are, together.

The suggestion, ready for a prompt: "One step for CL45+CL51: in `artifact_reconcile`, take the Artifact's side from the raw pulled file (`base/` as written by the load), not from the local board after `keep_newer`; keep `keep_newer` for the plain load on the web outside reconcile only if a test shows it cannot hide a both-sides change. A status lowered on the Artifact by a newer edit stands (a reopen is a change, not damage). Tests: `scripts/review/CR-cl45-…-seeded-conflict.py`'s five cases pass (seeded new container both dates, reopen, same container both dates). And a web review session never pushes board-mirror: set KIT_ROLE=review in the web review launch, or have reconcile read the session's role from its post."
